_comment: REQUIRED, not redundant with the repo-root .mcp.json. Verified 2026-08-25: with the repo mounted as a Cowork context folder, the repo-root .mcp.json produced no Playwright tools at all. Cowork does not read project-level .mcp.json; a plugin-bundled server is the only way it gets one. The repo copy serves Claude Code sessions rooted here. Keep the version pin identical in both. --output-dir is load-bearing: the server allows file uploads only from its output dir and its cwd, and Cowork spawns it with cwd=C:\Windows\System32, so without this the repo's own staged PDFs are rejected as "outside allowed roots". It also lets browser_evaluate write form-inventory manifests straight into the repo instead of through an agent's context. NOTHING IN THIS FILE TAKES EFFECT UNTIL THE PLUGIN IS REBUILT AND RE-UPLOADED: run `python scripts/build_cowork_plugin.py`, then Cowork tab -> Customize -> Plugins -> upload the zip. Cowork runs the snapshot it was given, and the installed copy is not readable from this machine, so an edit here that is never re-uploaded is invisible until a batch fails. That is exactly what happened on 2026-08-31: this file was correct, the installed plugin was a pre-4a7daae snapshot with no --output-dir, and seven applications were filed with no resume or cover letter attached. The batch preflight's upload probe is what catches it. The absolute path is machine-specific and intentional: the Playwright MCP server resolves --output-dir against its own cwd, which Cowork sets to C:\Windows\System32, so a relative path would point outside this repo. A path that works beats a portable one that does not.
